issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) defines Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String (message like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). The template Main.java also calls messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution introduces a Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) signature and implements it in Pig and Seal, requiring an int parameter. This mismatch between the expected no-arg method and the solution's parameterized method will confuse students and prevents them from matching the specification and the provided template usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the int parameter: declare Rideable.messageOnRide() and implement Pig/Seal.messageOnRide() with no parameters, returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"; or (B) If the speed parameter is intentional, update the problem statement UML/text and the template Main.java to document and call messageOnRide(int speed) (and adjust example outputs). Option A is recommended to align with the current specification and template.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and examples) defines Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String and the template Main code calls messageOnRide() with no arguments. The solution, however, defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements messageOnRide(int speed) in Pig and Seal. This introduces an extra parameter (speed) that is not present in the problem/template, creating a naming/signature mismatch that will confuse students about the required method signature and expected usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable API across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to implement messageOnRide() with no parameters (returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]") to match the UML/problem and template usage, or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnRide(int speed) (and update example return text to include speed). Prefer option A to preserve the UML and template expectations.
